skill.description: Use when creating, editing, or pressure-testing AI agent skills before deployment.
skill.summary: Guides test-driven skill writing, search optimization, and pre-deployment verification.
skill.author: Cycleaddict

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, inline paths, or broad keyword matches. Confirmed technical risk is limited to render-graphs.js, which invokes Graphviz through child_process and writes generated files under a user-selected skill directory. One semantic concern remains: the testing guidance teaches pressure-based prompts that should stay confined to explicit test harnesses.

remediation.issue: The Graphviz renderer executes external binaries from a bundled script.
remediation.suggestion: Document that render-graphs.js must only run on trusted skill directories, and require explicit user confirmation before invoking it.

remediation.issue: Generated SVG and DOT files are written under a user-supplied skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Print resolved output paths before writing, refuse unexpected targets, or add an explicit output directory option.

remediation.issue: Pressure-testing examples can be reused as agent manipulation prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Label these prompts as test fixtures only and warn authors not to use them in normal user interactions.

content.value_statement: Skill authors often ship unclear instructions that agents skip under pressure. This skill provides TDD-style writing and testing methods for reliable agent skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md structure, frontmatter, naming rules, and description triggers.
Maps test-driven development to skill creation with red, green, and refactor phases.
Provides Claude Search Optimization guidance for discoverable skill descriptions and keywords.
Includes pressure scenario methods for testing whether agents follow skills under constraints.
Documents flowchart guidance and includes a Graphviz renderer for DOT diagrams.
limitations: It does not automatically validate marketplace manifests or package metadata.
The Graphviz rendering helper requires a local dot installation.
The testing workflow can be excessive for simple reference-only skills.
Guidance is optimized for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill workflows.

use_cases.title: Draft a New Agent Skill
use_cases.description: Create a concise SKILL.md with strong triggers, clear rules, and useful supporting files.

use_cases.title: Improve Skill Discoverability
use_cases.description: Rewrite names, descriptions, and keywords so agents load the skill at the right time.

use_cases.title: Verify Skill Behavior Before Release
use_cases.description: Run pressure scenarios with subagents to check whether the skill prevents known failures.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a first skill draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a new agent skill for [topic]. Identify the trigger conditions, user goals, and one clear success criterion.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Discoverability
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for revising metadata and search terms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill description and title. Rewrite them so Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can decide when to load it.

prompt_templates.title: Create Pressure Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for validating skill compliance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three pressure scenarios that test whether an agent follows this skill under time, authority, and sunk-cost pressure.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Skill From Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for closing loopholes after testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Here are the failures from skill testing: [failures]. Update the skill guidance to close each loophole without adding unrelated content.

output_examples.input: A vague skill description that says it helps with testing.
output_examples.output: A trigger-focused description that names flaky behavior, race conditions, and timing failures.

output_examples.input: A draft skill with long background sections and repeated examples.
output: A short overview with the core principle.
A quick reference table for repeated decisions.
One practical example and a focused mistake list.

output_examples.input: A skill that agents ignore during urgent work.
output_examples.output: A pressure-test plan that records baseline failures, adds explicit counters, and re-tests compliance.

best_practices: Write the trigger description before expanding the body of the skill.
Run baseline pressure tests before adding rules that claim to prevent failures.
Keep supporting files only when they reduce main-document size or provide reusable tools.
anti_patterns: Do not summarize the full workflow in the description field.
Do not add multiple weak examples when one strong example is enough.
Do not deploy a discipline-focused skill without pressure testing it first.

faq.question: What type of skill does this help create?
faq.answer: It helps create agent skills that document reusable techniques, workflows, and reference material.

faq.question: Does it write the final skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives structure, quality checks, and testing methods for human-guided skill authoring.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance names Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill workflows.

faq.question: Why does it use TDD language?
faq.answer: It treats skill behavior as something to test before deployment, similar to software behavior.

faq.question: When should I skip pressure testing?
faq.answer: Skip it for pure reference skills with no behavior rules or compliance costs.

faq.question: What does the rendering script do?
faq.answer: It renders DOT flowcharts from SKILL.md into SVG files when Graphviz is installed.
